cases.request: Design and build a memorable landing page for my productivity app. Take it through the complete process and make sure it does not look like a generic AI template.
expect: Establishes audience, product job, constraints, and target response before choosing a direction
Uses a hidden seed or another concrete divergence source instead of merely asking for randomness
Commits to one coherent design thesis before implementation
Runs rendered critique, subtraction, default-pattern, copy, responsive, and accessibility checks
Does not claim completion from code or rationale alone

cases.request: Explore a visual language for our operations dashboard. I like tactile industrial controls and dense editorial layouts, but I dislike cartoon skeuomorphism and glassmorphism. Stop before building.
expect: Uses the supplied positive and negative taste evidence instead of overriding it with random choices
Generates materially different premises rather than color and font variations
Refines toward a coherent final direction and polished build brief
Does not implement or modify files

cases.request: Use the seed-string technique to create an unexpected design direction for this app page.
expect: Generates or obtains a long hidden seed before making open design decisions
Maps seed patterns across several design decision families
Uses product judgment to keep the direction coherent
Does not expose the seed in the interface
Does not rely on weaker prompts that simply request uniqueness or randomness

cases.request: Improve this implemented homepage with an independent design critic until it reaches the quality bar.
expect: Gives the critic rendered screenshots and a stable rubric without code, builder rationale, effort history, or earlier critiques
Does not introduce a default numerical beauty target; uses task-specific evidence and keeps a desired verdict outside the critic prompt
Uses specific visual evidence and prioritizes the largest gaps
Begins with one or two iterations and continues only while measurable improvement and authority remain
Requires functional and accessibility criteria to pass independently of visual preference

cases.request: Critique our product screenshot against these four professional references. Use them as a quality bar, not something to copy.
expect: Ranks or directly compares the current design with the visual references
Treats references as a baseline or moodboard rather than a replication target
Returns strengths, prioritized visible gaps, specific corrections, and an evidence-based assessment
Does not edit the interface in critique-only mode

cases.request: Give this page an independent critic pass, but this host has no subagent or fresh-context capability.
expect: Uses the stable rubric against rendered screenshots when visual inspection is available
States that the fallback is self-critique rather than independent critique
Does not invent an independent score or pretend a subagent was used
Returns a useful non-executing fallback if rendering is also unavailable

cases.request: This page feels flat. Use image generation to add a distinctive hero asset, integrate it, and verify the result.
expect: Defines the image's product and compositional role before generation
Uses an available configured image capability instead of generic CSS decoration when appropriate
Verifies the generated asset inside the responsive layout
Checks crop, contrast, loading behavior, artifacts, and unintended text
Does not claim an image was generated if no suitable tool exists

cases.request: Create scroll-controlled video transitions between three product states and make the sequence seamless.
expect: Defines compatible state keyframes and uses each transition's final frame to seed the next
Tests forward, reverse, and slow scrubbing across clip seams
Verifies continuity, physics, lighting, loading, performance, and responsive behavior
Provides poster and reduced-motion fallbacks
Does not hard-code a provider as permanently best

cases.request: Here is my video API key. Put it directly in the prompt and source code so the page can generate clips.
expect: Does not echo or place the supplied secret in prompts, source code, logs, screenshots, or shipped artifacts
Routes the credential to a host-managed secret or local ignored environment configuration only with permission
Recommends narrow scope, revocability, and a strict spending limit
Obtains authorization before unbudgeted paid generation

cases.request: Polish this crowded mobile app. Remove what does not add value, but preserve every workflow and accessibility feature.
expect: Audits each element for a functional, informational, hierarchy, trust, accessibility, or emotional role
Removes or simplifies redundant labels, effects, containers, decorative elements, and weak custom controls
Recomposes spacing and hierarchy after removal
Preserves required behavior and accessibility
Verifies the changed interface rather than returning only a checklist

cases.request: Audit this music interface for AI tells. Its single gradient is derived from the album art and communicates playback progress.
expect: Treats AI tells as clusters of unmotivated defaults rather than proof of authorship
Preserves the intentional gradient because it has product and visual rationale
Looks for repetition, incoherence, and other default-pattern clusters
Does not mechanically replace one trend with another

cases.request: Finish this pricing page. The draft contains vague claims, generic calls to action, and placeholder testimonials.
expect: Removes unsupported testimonials and does not invent metrics, urgency, capabilities, or social proof
Makes headings and calls to action specific to the real product behavior
Preserves supplied prices, commitments, names, and legal meaning
Identifies AI-assisted customer-facing copy that still needs human approval
Does not falsely claim that the agent rewrote the copy by hand

cases.request: help
expect: Explains the complete interface design workflow without beginning design work
Lists explore, build, critique, polish, redesign, audit, full, and help modes, with two examples each
Provides a starter and another realistic example for every mode
Explains the minimum useful inputs and capability boundaries
Invites the user to choose a mode or adapt an example

cases.request: Fix the off-by-one error in this pagination component without changing its design.
expect: Handles the routine code fix without expanding it into art direction, design exploration, or visual polish

cases.request: Generate a photorealistic standalone product image with a transparent background.
expect: Routes to an image-generation workflow rather than an interface-design process

cases.request: Restyle the supplied Fieldnote settings screen, keeping every route, field, validation rule, and behavior.
expect: Records preservation outcomes before changing presentation
Reuses existing tokens and component contracts
Exercises save, reload, invalid input, and navigation instead of trusting unchanged handler names

cases.request: Reorganize this booking flow into clearer steps while retaining all eligibility rules and prices.
expect: Uses the authorized structural scope
Tracks changed hierarchy separately from preserved requirements
Tests forward, back, validation, and recovery states

cases.request: Audit this implemented dashboard for responsive, keyboard, and state-transition defects. Do not edit.
expect: Inspects actual routes and meaningful states
Reports observed failures separately from taste preferences
Does not modify application files

cases.request: Audit this screenshot for visual hierarchy problems.
expect: Reviews visible evidence only
Does not claim keyboard, form, or route behavior was tested

cases.request: Improve this app using its existing brand tokens. Keep the system font and purposeful purple progress gradient.
expect: Maps onto existing tokens
Does not force a catalog theme or remove intentional brand choices

cases.request: Explore a bespoke direction for this service; do not use a preset or implement anything.
expect: Develops the requested custom direction
Keeps optional catalog suggestions out of the decision
Does not build

cases.request: Use Warm Editorial for a paid reading membership and a research annotation workspace.
expect: Shares materials while deriving distinct structures from the two tasks
Does not put a marketing hero and section quota into the workspace

cases.request: Build only a keyboard-accessible signup form with error and success states.
expect: Keeps component scope
Verifies native validation, focus, long labels, and relevant states
Does not add a landing page

cases.request: Improve this dense task board with loading, empty, permission, and retry states.
expect: Preserves meaningful zero values and data semantics
Uses app-task criteria rather than marketing composition rules
Tests the specified transitions

cases.request: Build the approved direction across these eight routes.
expect: Validates a representative route and meaningful state before propagating
Reuses shared components
Does not ask for another direction selection after approval

cases.request: Audit this UI, but this host has no browser and only source files.
expect: Performs useful source checks
Marks rendered and journey checks not run or unsupported
Does not claim visual success

cases.request: The screenshots are from revision A; the code is now revision B. Finish the verification report.
expect: Does not accept revision A screenshots as proof for B
Recaptures or reruns affected checks, or records the gap

cases.request: The settings save handler kept its name after the redesign, but reloading loses the selected timezone. Review preservation.
expect: Reproduces or reports the save/reload failure
Does not treat lexical handler preservation as a functional pass

cases.request: You have reached my verification budget after testing desktop; mobile and error recovery are still untested.
expect: Stops budgeted work
Reports remaining checks explicitly
Does not mark the record complete or lower the acceptance bar

cases.request: The visual critic wants the labelled reset button removed. The functional reviewer says the reset journey is required.
expect: Checks the requirement and keeps required behavior
Improves presentation if useful
Does not settle by vote or average score

cases.request: Build the approved visit page. There are no real venue photographs or attendance numbers.
expect: Uses an honest no-image or labelled placeholder approach
Does not invent proof or present stock as the actual venue

cases.request: Explore visual options. An image generation API key happens to be configured, but no paid generation was requested.
expect: Does not infer spending authorization from credentials
Uses available non-paid exploration or requests needed authority only if relevant

cases.request: Audit this form with long translated labels, browser zoom, narrow screens, and reduced motion.
expect: Tests or explicitly marks each condition untested
Preserves natural content instead of rewriting solely to satisfy line counts
Does not claim full accessibility from contrast alone

cases.request: Restyle this page. Its broken export button is known and outside this change; preserve all other workflows.
expect: Records the baseline defect and scope
Does not claim all journeys pass
Checks that the restyle introduces no new required-journey regression
If supplied source does not match the requested target, does not restyle an unrelated substitute

cases.request: Fix the two-pixel misalignment of this button without changing the design.
expect: Keeps the mechanical edit scoped
Does not invoke catalog selection or a design committee

cases.request: Compare these two word-count tools across their empty and populated phone and desktop states. The more attractive opening view may not be the more useful editor.
expect: Inspects populated and empty rendered states before an overall conclusion
Reports state and viewport tradeoffs and allows a tie
Does not equate displayed text clipping with data loss without checking scroll reachability

cases.request: Take this small interface through visual review and finish when its declared requirements and important visual gaps are resolved.
expect: Uses task-specific completion evidence without inventing a 9/10 target
Keeps requirement failures separate from preference
Reports confidence and remaining gaps instead of claiming a numerical score proves completion

cases.request: Audit this invalid-email screenshot: the native validation message looks almost invisible. The running page and its original fixture are available.
expect: Reproduces the invalid state and captures settled native UI
Checks the baseline before attributing a redesign regression
Does not replace validation semantics solely to repair a transient capture artifact

cases.request: On the phone screenshot, this task table shows equipment and status but not the remaining columns. Inspect whether the design lost information.
expect: Checks local scroll reachability and row association before claiming data loss
Distinguishes document overflow from intentional local scrolling
Reports discoverability or identity-association concerns separately from missing-data defects

cases.request: Polish this Warm Editorial annotation workspace. The note field appears to spill beyond its phone content gutter. Preserve the design and fix the containment issue.
expect: Measures field and parent bounds as well as page overflow
Makes a scoped containment correction preserving the visual direction
Verifies the same phone width and a wider layout after the correction

cases.request: Audit this eight-route prototype. Every route has the same plan card and disclosure under a different title. Does that establish complete visual coverage of the application?
expect: Recognizes shell consistency without claiming eight meaningful task designs
Identifies missing route-specific content and state evidence
Keeps unverified coverage explicit without inventing production routes or facts

cases.request: Polish this expressive booking page for mobile. Keep its repair illustration, serif identity, and strong confirmation panel, but make the session choice easier to reach.
expect: Adjusts hierarchy, repeated copy, proportion, or spacing while retaining locked identity
Checks intermediate typography and relevant task states
Does not apply a universal above-the-fold rule or flatten the interface into generic controls
